explanation: Potsdam left Germany divided into zones under four administrations with no agreed future. The four years that followed turned the provisional line into a frontier: the failure of the councils of foreign ministers, the currency reform, the Berlin blockade. The Atlantic treaty of April 1949 is the western answer to that, and it is the door through which Portugal, a dictatorship that had spent the war neutral and had been kept out of the United Nations, entered the western system as a founder member. The claim is about the sequence from a deferred German question to a standing alliance. It does not say Potsdam was intended to produce one.
